studies.Reference: Intake of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids and risk of ovarian cancer.
studies.Authors: Ibiebele TI, Nagle CM, Bain CJ, Webb PM
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Participants in the Australian Ovarian Cancer Study (1,366 cases and 1,414 population controls) self-completed risk factor and food frequency questionnaires.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Participants in the Australian Ovarian Cancer Study (1,366 cases and 1,414 population controls).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: High intake of total n-6 fatty acids was inversely associated with risk (OR for highest vs. lowest category 0.78).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: High intake of total n-6 fatty acids was inversely associated with risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: evaluate the role of polyunsaturated fatty acids in ovarian carcinogenesis.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: High intake of total n-6 fatty acids.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Insufficient studies to perform formal publication bias testing.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.8 (95% CI: 0.69–0.91), suggesting that omega-6 fatty acids is associated with a lower risk of ovarian cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
